qaPairs.q: Define liquefaction and state how it is achieved experimentally.
qaPairs.answer: A physical process that converts a gaseous mixture into a liquid. Achieved by increasing the pressure or decreasing the temperature of the gas.

qaPairs.q: Explain why carbon dioxide and water vapour must be completely removed during purification before air undergoes liquefaction at -200°C.
qaPairs.answer: At -80°C, carbon dioxide and water vapour solidify into solids. If not removed, these solids will block/clog the pipes and fractionating equipment during the liquefaction process at -200°C.

dissolutionPrinciple.q: Why is water a good solvent for NaCl?
markingPoints: NaCl has a giant ionic lattice structure held by strong ionic bonds.
Water is a polar molecule with partial negative charge on oxygen and partial positive charge on hydrogen.
The energy released during hydration is sufficient to overcome the strong ionic bonds in the NaCl lattice.

crystallizationMethods.caution: Do NOT heat to complete dryness as boiling can cause solute decomposition or spurting.

steps: Allow saturated solution to cool down slowly to room temperature.
Filter and wash crystals with small amount of cold distilled water.

products.uses: Making soap, drain cleaner, neutralizing acidic effluents

limewaterTest.q: When SO2 gas is bubbled into calcium hydroxide solution for a short period, state the expected observation and equation.
limewaterTest.reason: SO2 reacts with Ca(OH)2 to form an insoluble white precipitate CaSO3.

metallicBonding.q: Why do metals have high melting points and good electrical conductivity?
metallicBonding.structure: Giant metallic structure with strong non-directional electrostatic attraction between metal cations and delocalized electrons.
metallicBonding.conductivity: Delocalized electrons are free to move throughout the lattice to transfer charge/heat.
metallicBonding.malleability: Metal cations are packed in layers. When force is applied, layers slide over each other without breaking metallic bonds.

qaPairs.q: Why is electrolysis of molten metal ores expensive?
qaPairs.answer:
1. Huge consumption of electricity for electrolysis.
2. Huge consumption of fuel for heating to maintain molten state.

qaPairs.q: Why should molten state of ore be used instead of solid state?
qaPairs.answer: Molten metal ores contain mobile ions which can conduct electricity, while solid state cannot.

qaPairs.q: Why remove copper(II) ions from wastewater before discharge?
qaPairs.answer:
1. To reduce the loss of copper metal.
2. Copper(II) ions are toxic and cause water pollution.

atomicRadiusExplanation.q: Why is Sodium (Na) more reactive than Magnesium (Mg)?
atomicRadiusExplanation.answer: Sodium has a larger atomic radius than Magnesium, so it loses its outermost shell electron more readily.

group1Observations: Metal melts into a silvery ball and floats/moves rapidly on water surface.
Solution turns pink when phenolphthalein is added (alkaline NaOH formed).

pbSulfuricAcidAnomaly.q: Why does reaction between Lead (Pb) and dilute H2SO4 stop quickly?
pbSulfuricAcidAnomaly.answer: Pb reacts with H2SO4 to form an insoluble layer of Lead(II) sulphate (PbSO4). This insoluble layer covers the metal surface and prevents further reaction.

displacementReactions.principle: An atom of a more reactive metal loses electrons more readily to form cations. Cations of the less reactive metal accept electrons and deposit as metal atoms.

electrolyteRole.q: Why add NaCl before conducting displacement in water?
electrolyteRole.answer: NaCl acts as an electrolyte providing mobile ions to improve electrical conductivity.

polymer.name: addition polymerisation
babySteps: • ❰ X ❱ (addition polymerisation) involves random chain termination.
• Different polymer chains stop growing at different times, giving ❰ Y ❱ (different chain lengths).
• Therefore the polymer has a range of relative molecular masses rather than one fixed value.
